REI’s Holiday Sale runs through Nov. 23, and the co-op’s men’s and women’s clothing and footwear deal pages list more than 5,000 marked-down items between them. You can browse everything on the men’s deals page and the women’s deals page, where many REI Co-op jackets, fleece, base layers and pants are 25% off and outside brands run from Burton to Danner. REI members can also save 20% on one full-price item and one REI Outlet item with code HOLIDAY2026 through Nov. 23 (terms apply). We checked every price in this post on REI.com Monday afternoon, November 16.

Real down insulation for less than $100.

Industry observers note that the REI Co-op 650 Down Jacket (men’s) is $96.69 (was $129) through Nov. 23, which puts a 650-fill-power down jacket under $100. REI lists the men’s version at 10.9 ounces, with a windproof, water-resistant recycled ripstop nylon shell, two zippered hand pockets and two interior drop-in pockets. The women’s version is the same $96.69 (was $129) and weighs 10.2 ounces by REI’s count. REI pitches it for cool weather rather than deep cold, so our guide to the best winter jackets is the better starting point for subzero mornings.

In a recent development, midweight merino with a sale that runs through Nov. 30.

This one gets an extra week. The Smartwool Classic Thermal Merino Crew Base Layer Top (men’s) is $93.69 (was $125) through Nov. 30, according to REI, while the Holiday Sale ends Nov. 23. Smartwool knits it from 250-weight merino interlock, and the updated design swaps shoulder seams for shoulder panels, so a pack strap has no seam to press on. The matching bottoms are also $93.69 through Nov. 30.

Waterproof hikers that weigh under 2 pounds a pair.

Hiking boots don’t have to feel like ankle weights. REI lists the Merrell Moab Speed 2 Mid GORE-TEX Hiking Boots (men’s) at 1 pound, 12.2 ounces per pair, with a Gore-Tex membrane, Merrell’s FloatPro foam midsole and a Vibram TC5+ outsole with 4mm lugs. They’re $138.69 (was $185) through Nov. 23. REI’s fit note claims they run slightly large, and our hiking boot guide rounds up more options.

In a recent development, the REI Co-op 650 Down Jacket is covered above, and REI’s own insulated jackets show up all over this category. The REI Co-op Microtrek Insulated Hoodie (women’s) is $134.19 (was $179), and the Marmot Highlander Down Hoody (men’s) is $184.73 (was $250) at REI Outlet.

Synthetic fill and a DWR shell for under $90.

Synthetic insulation holds up better than down when it gets wet, so the REI Co-op Trailmade Insulated Hoodie (men’s) makes sense for soggy winters. It’s $89.19 (was $119) through Nov. 23. REI pairs the synthetic fill with a polyester shell treated with a PFAS-free DWR finish, and the men’s version weighs 1 pound, 3.8 ounces. The women’s version is also $89.19 (was $119).

The REI Co-op Trailmade Rain Jacket (women’s) is the cheapest pick here at $59.89 (was $79.95). Cotopaxi’s Cielo Rain Trench Jacket (women’s) is $157.49 (was $210) for a longer cut, and the REI Co-op Teris GTX Rain Jacket (men’s) brings a Gore-Tex shell down to $194.19 (was $259).

Pit zips and a 2.5-layer shell for under $75.

Industry observers note that the REI Co-op Rainier Rain Jacket (men’s) is $74.89 (was $99.95) through Nov. 23, and the women’s version matches it. REI builds it with a 2.5-layer recycled ripstop shell and a HydroWall membrane, rates it windproof up to 60 mph, and adds pit zips for climbs where you’d otherwise sweat through your base layer. The men’s jacket weighs 11.3 ounces, and our packable rain jacket guide has more picks.

It has been revealed that both Burton jackets in this section are half off in select colors, starting with the Burton Reserve 2L Insulated Jacket (men’s) at $144.83 (was $289.95). The Obermeyer Raze Insulated Jacket (men’s) is $224.73 (was $329) at REI Outlet.

Bibs with thigh vents and built-in boot gaiters.

In a recent development, bibs keep snow out of your waistband on deep days, and the REI Co-op Powderbound Insulated Bib Snow Pants (men’s) are $164.19 (was $219) through Nov. 23. REI uses a two-layer waterproof, breathable laminate with critically taped seams, 40 grams of recycled synthetic insulation, inner thigh vents, and boot gaiters with grippy elastic. They come in short, regular and tall inseams (29.5, 32 and 35 inches).

Recent findings suggest that every fleece here costs less than $100. The REI Co-op Trailmade Fleece Jacket (men’s) is the cheapest at $52.39 (was $69.95), and the Free Country Sierra Sherpa Fleece Pile Snap-Front Jacket (women’s) is $62.73 (was $95) at REI Outlet.

Light recycled Polartec fleece for layering.

The Fjällräven Kaipak Fleece Jacket (women’s) is $62.99 (was $90) through Nov. 23. Fjällräven uses recycled Polartec fleece for the body and its G-1000 Air fabric on the zippered chest pocket, with zippered hand pockets and raglan sleeves. At 8.8 ounces by REI’s count, it fits under a rain shell without much bulk.

The Smartwool Classic Thermal Merino Crew Base Layer Top (men’s) is covered above. REI’s Midweight Long-Sleeve Crew Base Layer Top (men’s) is the cheapest option at $48.69 (was $64.95), and the Smartwool Classic All-Season Merino Long-Sleeve Base Layer Top (men’s) is $74.99 (was $100) through Nov. 30.

Lightweight 100% merino for under $65.

It has been revealed that the REI Co-op Merino 185 Long-Sleeve Crew Base Layer Top (men’s) is $63.69 (was $84.95) through Nov. 23. It’s 100% merino wool at 185 grams per square meter, which REI classifies as lightweight, so it works as a next-to-skin layer on cold hikes and as a plain long-sleeve tee the rest of the week. REI also rates it UPF 30. The matching bottoms are $63.69 (was $84.95) too.

REI’s Active Pursuits line covers the cheap end, starting with the REI Co-op Active Pursuits T-Shirt (men’s) at $24.39 (was $34.95). For flannel season, the Patagonia Fjord Flannel Shirt (men’s) is $74.97 (was $119) at REI Outlet.

A sun-blocking long-sleeve tee for under $30.

Sources indicate that the REI Co-op Active Pursuits Long-Sleeve T-Shirt (men’s) is $27.89 (was $39.95) through Nov. 23. REI makes it from a 92% polyester, 8% spandex knit, rates it UPF 50+, and lists hiking, running and fitness as its best uses. REI’s fit note says it runs slightly large.

It has been revealed that the Free Country Trail 2 Town Flare Pants (women’s) are $44.73 (was $68) at REI Outlet, and the Nani Trekker Pants (women’s) are $69.93 (was $94). The Powderbound bibs are in the snow section above.

Stretchy nylon trail pants with a zip thigh pocket.

The REI Co-op Trailmade Pants (men’s) are $59.89 (was $79.95) through Nov. 23. REI cuts them from a 96% nylon, 4% spandex blend with a PFAS-free DWR finish and UPF 50+ sun protection, and the zippered thigh pocket gives a phone a secure spot. They come in 30-, 32- and 34-inch inseams.

Recent findings suggest that the Merrell Moab Speed 2 Mid GORE-TEX Hiking Boots (men’s) are covered above. The Altra Timp 5 Hiker GTX Hiking Boots (women’s) are $134.73 (was $180) at REI Outlet, and the Oboz Sawtooth Ascent Mid Waterproof Hiking Boots (men’s) are $131.19 (was $175). The Danner Mountain 600 Leaf GTX Hiking Boots (men’s) stay on sale through Dec. 4.

Nubuck leather boots with a waterproof membrane.

If you want a traditional leather boot, the KEEN Targhee IV Mid Waterproof Hiking Boots (men’s) are $142.49 (was $190) through Nov. 23. KEEN pairs a nubuck leather upper with its KEEN.DRY waterproof membrane, and REI lists them at 2 pounds, 8.6 ounces per pair, about 12 ounces heavier than the lightweight boots above. REI’s fit note says they run slightly large.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

In a recent development, FINDING A GIFT for dad can be a daunting task in the countdown to the holidays. If you have siblings, you especially know what we mean—there's an unspoken competition to see who can impress dad the most.

What makes a cool gift for dad these days? Well, on top of balancing a fine line between trendy and functional, new and nostalgic, the gifts we've curated are sure to answer a certain calling or scratch an itch he's had for some time. We've gathered an array of remarkable gifts for men, from adjustable (and affordable) kettlebells to a scoreboard ticker to a cozy bathrobe.

This list is dynamic because that's exactly what fathers are. And it's varied too, also just like all those old men out there. We've got running shoes for jogging dads, gadgets for DIY dads, literature for bookworm dads, and excellent food for hungry dads. He's sure to unwrap something that he will spend a lot of quality time with, right out of the gate.

They don’t have to be a renowned angler to appreciate a good fishing shirt: They’re stretchy, quick drying, and moisture wicking. Huckberry made this elevated version that can go from the boat to the bar using a lightweight nylon fabric. The double pockets and western yoke are subtle nods to heritage workwear.

It has been revealed that this handwoven hammock chair beats his favorite lawn chair by a mile. The acrylic yarn won’t fade, mold, or rot, and the colors stay vibrant without fading. More than a chair, there’s plenty of room to sprawl out for a midday nap or to catch up on a book. Spring for the stand, and they can take this chair anywhere.

According to recent reports, every childhood memory I have of my dad coming home from work includes a pen—he had at least two in the chest pocket of his button-up shirt—and he still keeps one strapped to his wrist today. A reliable pen may seem novel in an increasingly digital world, but that’s what makes it (even more) gift-worthy. The Lamy 2000 has a satisfying click, good looks, and a smooth ballpoint for all his notes and scribbles.

In a recent development, the Pacebreakers are an excellent do-everything pair of shorts: he can work out, chill out, even swim in them if he’s in a pinch. They come in a bunch of different colors and are available in 5-, 7-, and 9-inch inseams. Hard to find a better pair of active shorts out there.

Recent findings suggest that A reliable pocket knife comes in handy more often than you think. While he may have his go-to, the Benchmade Bugout is sure to impress with its attention to detail and American-made craftsmanship. The Grivory handle is lightweight and grippy, and the drop point blade has excellent edge retention. It’s a slick addition to the old man’s EDC.

Sources indicate that “Give them something they’ll actually use”—a good starting point when thinking of what to gift a picky dad. Now think about how many times he uses the bathroom. You see where we’re going with this? The Tushy Wave is the brand's most elevated non-electric attachment, and it’ll keep the old man fresh. It’s a snap to set up, easy to use, and will save him money on toilet paper.

The garage is a sacred place for dads where they can have everything, particularly in or out of place, as they want. These Payloader boxes from Decked will have his tools, gear, and seasonal needs all organized and protected. They’re extremely durable, feature a snap-lock lid, and are made in the U.S.A.

What dad doesn’t love a significant screen? The MoGo 4 projector delivers a crisp 1080p display so he can project movies, matches, and demonstrates anywhere he pleases. Auto-adjust features make it easy to use, and onboard Google TV, Netflix, and YouTube makes streaming seamless. The projector itself is about the size of a coffee tumbler for easy storage, and onboard speakers mean he doesn’t have to hassle with an external set.

Sources indicate that patagonia’s Black Hole bags are widely popular for good reason—they’re durable, weather-resistant, and look cool. The nylon fabric resists tears and abrasions, and the multiple pockets hold everything he may need. It can double as a large gym bag as easily as it can take him on a weekend getaway. The Black Hole duffle comes in various sizes and colors to suit exactly what he wants.

Sources indicate that for the dad who loves making drinks at home and wants to impress his friends, this cult-favorite book from Death & Co. is packed with more than 500 cocktail recipes, bartending tips, and insider tricks from one of NYC’s most famous bars. His home bar setup will instantly feel a whole lot cooler.

Recent findings suggest that many speakers can go outside, but Turtlebox is built for it. The Ranger is a fully waterproof speaker that is loud enough to fill the entire backyard. It doesn’t just turn up to the loudest possible decibel, though; it actually sounds good with a deep base and no tinny noises on the high end.

In a recent development, nothing beats lazing around in a plushy bathrobe, but the summer months call for something a little more breezy. Brooklinen took its ultra-popular bathrobe and shortened it to let some air in on those legs. Even if he already has a bathrobe, consider this his summer style.

DIY projects are not just a game of inches; they can come down to millimeters and more. Give dad some exactness with this great laser measure. It looks ultra-modern and will make his crafty work all the more, according to initiative. It has a range of more than 90 feet and connects right to an app for real-time figures.

If Dad's always on his phone checking scores, there's a better way. Gift him this cool LED ticker, featuring a pixelated scoreboard built around his top squads. It's like a Lite-Brite set for the sports enthusiast. We've found it's great beyond just tailgating season, too, as you can get news blurbs and weather info, among other things.

Sources indicate that we love a good adjustable gym tool. This kettlebell can evolve with his workouts, spanning a weight range of 32 pounds and effectively replacing six individual weights. There's even an associated app with workouts if dad needs a nudge of inspiration to really get going.

Honestly, we were a bit skeptical of this muscle and nerve stimulator. Until we tried it out, and fell for the multiple settings and massage-like treatments that can target very specific areas. There's a precision to the Halo, and it makes recovery all the more enjoyable, not to mention rejuvenating.

Dad taught you all those things; why not return the favor? Go with the wisdom of a real pro, whether it's a culinary figure, an actor, a scientist, or some other notable person. He'll love being a student again. And the number of teachers just keeps growing, in both numbers and professions.

In a recent development, if he's going to cook that meat, set him up with a proper thermometer. Digital is the way to go, as it's more accurate and much easier to deal with. Plus, that'll make less risk of undercooking anything. Even dad can use an assist on the grill from time-to-time. This one won us over by freeing up valuable time as the app will essentially babysit you cooking proteins for you.

Read More: Best Kitchen Gadgets.

Recent findings suggest that let us generalize a bit here. Dads like fires and they also like DIY. Well, this might be the perfect scratch for those itches, a pizza maker from Solo Stove. ACOG Strongly Recommends Hormone Therapy for Menopause Symptoms

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) published updated recommendations for menopause management in Obstetrics & Gynecology on October 15.
  • Recent findings suggest that these expanded recommendations are the most comprehensive guidance to date.
  • According to the ACOG guidance, 50%–92% of females experiencing menopause report VMS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) published updated recommendations for menopause management in Obstetrics & Gynecology on October 15.

Recent findings suggest that these expanded recommendations are the most comprehensive guidance to date. They include upcoming clinical guidelines for menopause hormone therapy (MHT), nonhormonal medications, and nonpharmacological treatment of vasomotor symptoms (VMS), which include hot flashes and night sweats, and sleep and mood changes.

According to the ACOG guidance, 50%–92% of females experiencing menopause report VMS.

Around 16%–66% of females in the United States report menopause-related sleep complications, and more than one-third of perimenopausal and postmenopausal females report experiencing depressive symptoms.

“In recent years, misconceptions about the risks of hormone therapy have been widespread, which has made some clinicians reluctant to prescribe it and some patients hesitant to use it,” Bruce Pier, MD, clinical professor and associate fellowship director at the University of North Carolina and collaborator on the ACOG clinical practice guidelines, told Healthline.

“This guidance offers a comprehensive review of the evidence to support individualized counseling and shared decision making. Our hope is that it clears up those misconceptions and expands access to treatment.”.

The ACOG is also developing companion guidance for genitourinary syndrome of menopause, expected in 2027.

The ACOG strongly recommends the use of MHT with estrogen and progestogens (or estrogen alone for people without a uterus) for both VMS and vasomotor-related sleep disturbance, in individuals who can use hormones.

It also conditionally recommends conjugated estrogen plus bazedoxifene (Duavee) as an alternative for these complications.

Recent findings suggest that according to a meta-analysis from 2021 that was cited by the guidelines, estrogen therapy, with or without progestogens, significantly reduced VMS frequency and severity compared to a placebo or no treatment. A 2017 meta-analysis ranked transdermal estradiol plus a progestogen as the most effective option for reducing VMS frequency.

A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis, also cited by the guidelines, found that MHT was associated with improved self-reported sleep quality. Once again, transdermal therapies showed some of the largest effects.

The ACOG recommends initiating MHT before age 60 or within 10 years of the onset of natural menopause..

In a recent development, it also suggests that the decision to start MHT for VMS and vasomotor-related sleep disturbances should be based on a shared decision making discussion about an individual’s symptoms and the benefits and risks of therapy. Consideration should also be taken regarding an individual’s:.

Research demonstrates that factors such as race, culture, socioeconomic status, gender identity, and sexual orientation can influence how individuals experience menopause and the care they receive.

According to the SWAN study, Black women reported more menopause symptoms than white women but were less likely to be treated for them.

Recent findings suggest that “This updated document shines a light on these inequities. Clinicians can proactively help right now by asking every patient in midlife about symptoms, rather than waiting for them to bring it up. Long term, we hope this document drives more research funding to understand these gaps and begin closing them,” said Pier.

The ACOG stated in the guidelines that, “The available evidence is insufficient to recommend for or against the use of estrogen–progestogen or estrogen-only MHT for the treatment of menopause-related depressive symptoms.”.

It recommends that perimenopausal and postmenopausal individuals who meet the diagnostic criteria for major depressive disorder (MDD) or those whose most noticeable symptom is depression should be treated according to depression management guidelines.

Current treatment guidelines for depression include therapy, medication, or a combination of the two.

Psychological treatments for depression include psychotherapy, such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), while antidepressants are among the most commonly prescribed medications.

The ACOG strongly recommends the use of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) for the management of menopausal symptoms like VMS and depression in individuals who don’t want to use MHT or can’t use it.

Presently, paroxetine is the only antidepressant that is approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the management of VMS.

The ACOG also strongly recommends the use of neurokinin receptor antagonists to manage VMS and vasomotor-related sleep disturbances in people who don’t desire hormone therapy or can’t use it.

There are right now two neurokinin receptor antagonists approved by the FDA to manage menopause symptoms. Fezolinetant (Veozah) was approved in 2023 to help manage hot flashes. In 2025, the FDA approved elinzanetant (LYNKUET) for the management of moderate to severe VMS due to menopause.

Another nonhormonal treatment for VMS that the ACOG conditionally recommends is gabapentin.

There are various nonpharmacologic treatments that the ACOG conditionally recommends for the management of VMS, vasomotor-related sleep disturbances, and mood changes. These are treatments that don’t involve the use of medications.

The nonpharmacologic treatments conditionally recommended include:.

It is generally recommended that these interventions are used alongside hormonal or nonhormonal medications.

The ACOG noted that there is not enough evidence to support the efficacy or safety of phytoestrogens, such as soy isoflavones, or herbal supplements, which are not regulated by the FDA in the same way medications are for safety, purity, or efficacy.

Industry observers note that “Menopause is finally getting the attention it deserves, and this document shows what evidence-based care should look like in this space. It lays out a range of safe, effective options for managing menopause symptoms. My message to anyone struggling with these symptoms is simple: talk to your clinician. You don’t have to suffer through them,” mentioned Pier.

Storage Features: The storage bed you select should align with your space. If you're tight on floor space, consider a storage bed that lifts up. If you have low ceilings, consider a storage bed that has drawers underneath.

In a recent development, durability: We tested storage beds by sleeping on them night after night, taking notice of any factors like creakiness or wobbliness. We also looked for options with high-quality materials like fine upholstery and solid wood that are designed to last.

Price: Storage beds run from a few hundred dollars to well over $2,000, and our picks span that whole range. While the price isn't always the biggest indicator of quality, materials like bouclé and solid wood are usually found in more high-end storage beds.

What Are the Different Types of Storage Beds?

In a recent development, lift-up beds: Also called an "ottoman bed," this is a model where the mattress base lifts up with the aid of gas struts (pressurized cylinders that do most of the lifting for you), which retailers often call hydraulic lifts. This typically offers the most room out of the storage bed options.

Drawer beds: Fairly self-explanatory: drawers (either under, alongside, or at the foot of the bed) are this frame’s storage approach.

Recent findings suggest that headboard storage beds: A headboard storage bed draws from mid-century styles, where built-in shelves or nightstands create storage opportunities. This is a good option if what you need to store is also aesthetically pleasing.

Cubby beds: Instead of drawers, these cubbies are open shelving solutions underneath the bed frame, particularly suitable for holding books if you’re looking for a stylish way to create a bedroom library.

What’s a “Hydraulic Lift” in a Storage Bed?

Recent findings suggest that when your storage bed has interior storage (in other words, when you lift the mattress base upward to access its storage), it needs a lift mechanism to make it possible for you to lift the bed without breaking your back, and to keep the slatted frame upright while you lift your items in and out. Most use gas struts, though you'll often see them sold as hydraulic. If your storage bed has interior storage and no lift, you will collapse yourself and ultimately be pancaked by your own sleep-and-store investment.

What Features Should I Look for in the Best Storage Beds?

A good storage bed, in our opinion, doesn't look like a storage bed. It looks like a regular bed. It's crafted from, ideally, kiln-dried hardwood, it has a slatted base so you don't need to bother with a box spring, and it has non-sticky drawers (thank you, Thuma) or a lift mechanism to help with the lifting of interior storage (thank you, Saatva). Look for a solid wood base, linen upholstery, and invest in some vacuum-sealed bags. I live by these.

What Materials Make a Good Storage Bed?

Industry observers note that you're primarily searching for durability and space in storage bed models. Look for frames made from solid wood since this type of material is typically sturdy and long-lasting. A lift mechanism makes storage more accessible without back-breaking exercises. While upholstered beds are a popular favorite, make sure what lies beneath the textile is also going to stand the test of time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet. You’ve probably seen at least a few videos of the birds on social media darting across beaches and being incredibly vocal. As if their small, squat bodies and comically long beaks weren’t enough, they also vocalize with distinctively cartoonish peeping tweets during their mating displays.

Recent findings suggest that woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances. Six of the eight species are only found on specific islands, and some of them don’t even migrate at all. So how did these evolutionary oddballs even get their start—and stop migrating? To piece together their unique avian story, biologists analyzed the DNA of all eight woodcock species and 22 species of snipe.

Industry observers note that “The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, stated in a statement. “They’re not terribly aerodynamic, and yet they’ve clearly gotten around.”.

Bates and his colleagues published the results of their work today in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS). The years-long endeavor involved not only examining preserved woodcock specimens housed in the Field Museum, but a fossilized sandpiper previously excavated from a cave site in Haiti. The remains found on the island of Hispaniola are around 1,000 years old, but that is still extremely young in the grand history of shorebirds.

In a recent development, the earliest members of the sandpiper family began in the northern hemisphere before slowly migrating to islands along lower latitudes. Those birds subsequently migrated much shorter distances after settling in the warmer climates. However, they didn’t remain sedentary. Based on the DNA analysis detailed in their study, Bates and his team theorize that snipes from Africa eventually traveled across the Atlantic Ocean, then evolved into new species in South America. From there, more of the birds made their way over the Pacific Ocean to New Zealand.

Their examinations also cleared up a bit of confusion. Biologists initially believed the fossilized sandpiper from Haiti was a woodcock, but the most recent data now indicates that it’s a snipe.

Industry observers note that “Snipes and woodcocks have been around for 20 to 25 million years,” Bates explained. “Over that time, as new species have evolved and moved around the world, their migratory patterns have changed, too.”.

These changes are likely to continue amid today’s dramatic climate shifts, but that may pose a problem for the beloved woodcocks.

According to recent reports, “These are definitely birds that would be affected by changing habitats and changing climates,” remarked Bates. “Some of these woodcocks are found only in the mountain forests on islands between Asia and Australia, and if those forests get cut down, the birds are going to be gone too.”.

Christina Applegate shared an unexpected health revision on her return to the MeSsy podcast with co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler.

The two actors have detailed their experiences with multiple sclerosis (MS), a neurological disorder that can lead to debilitating symptoms affecting daily functioning and quality of life.

Applegate, 54, has been raising awareness about the condition since her initial diagnosis in 2021.

In two podcast episodes released October 20, Applegate revealed that doctors had told her she was misdiagnosed with MS.

According to recent reports, “She came into my room and remarked, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,’ ” Applegate said as she fought back tears. “I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”.

The “Anchorman” and “Dead to Me” actor explained that her symptoms have continued to worsen, leaving her without an explanation for what she’s experiencing as doctors investigate the cause.

Recent findings suggest that being misdiagnosed with MS is relatively common. Applegate’s revelation highlights a difficult reality for people living with unexplained symptoms resembling MS. Her experience raises questions about how MS is diagnosed, why misdiagnoses may occur, and what people can do when their symptoms don’t match their diagnosis.

While MS can be difficult to diagnose, an accurate diagnosis can help people with the condition gain access to appropriate treatment. A misdiagnosis, on the other hand, may lead to unnecessary interventions and medication, and take an emotional toll over time.

“MS can be challenging to diagnose because there is no single test that confirms it in every case,” stated Steve Allder, MD, consultant neurologist at Re:Cognition Health.

“An incorrect diagnosis can have significant consequences. Someone incorrectly diagnosed with MS may experience considerable anxiety, undergo unnecessary investigations, or receive treatments with potential risks and side effects. Equally, if MS is missed, treatment may be delayed, potentially allowing further neurological damage,” Allder told Healthline.

A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis underscores that MS misdiagnoses remain a concern.

Research suggests that around 15% of people diagnosed with MS may actually have another condition.

However, estimates vary across studies, with some reporting rates ranging from 5–41%.

While an accurate diagnosis can guide patients toward appropriate treatment, a mistaken one may lead to unnecessary medication, emotional distress, and years of uncertainty.

Fresh diagnostic guidelines offer hope for greater accuracy, but they also raise crucial questions about how doctors can adequately distinguish MS from other conditions.

“Research has shown that MS can be both overdiagnosed and underdiagnosed,” Allder remarked.

According to recent reports, “Diagnosis relies on a combination of symptoms, neurological examination, MRI findings, and sometimes, additional tests. It is also important to recognize that diagnoses can evolve as fresh evidence emerges. As neurologists, we must remain open to revisiting a diagnosis when symptoms or test results do not fit, ensuring patients receive appropriate treatment and support.”.

It has been revealed that MS symptoms may vary widely and overlap with several other conditions. These may include:.

Because these conditions share certain features with MS, healthcare professionals should consider a patient’s full clinical profile rather than relying on a single symptom or scan.

“MS can cause numbness, tingling, muscle weakness, visual disturbances, balance problems, and fatigue. However, these symptoms are not unique to the condition,” Allder said.

“For example, numbness and tingling may indicate peripheral neuropathy, sometimes associated with diabetes or vitamin B12 deficiency. Weakness or altered sensation may result from a trapped nerve or spinal cord compression. Migraines can cause visual disturbances and sensory symptoms, while inner-ear disorders may affect balance,” he continued.

Allder noted that fatigue is particularly nonspecific and may be associated with:.

He explained that, as a neurologist, he considers the pattern, duration, and progression of symptoms alongside examination findings.

“No single symptom automatically indicates MS. A thorough assessment is essential to identify the underlying cause and ensure the patient receives appropriate treatment,” he said.

There is no single test that definitively confirms every case of MS.

Diagnosis typically involves reviewing symptoms, conducting neurological examinations, and evaluating MRI scans and laboratory results.

MRI findings may be tricky to interpret. Some white-matter spots resemble MS lesions but may result from migraine, aging, or other conditions. Misapplying diagnostic criteria or overlooking alternative explanations can also lead to mistakes.

“MRI abnormalities alone do not confirm MS,” Allder stated. “The diagnosis must be based on the overall clinical picture, with alternative explanations carefully considered.”.

Research also suggests that MS misdiagnosis rates may differ by sex.

Research shows females are 2.1 times more likely to be misdiagnosed with MS than males, highlighting the potential for diagnostic bias and differences in how symptoms are evaluated.

The updated MS diagnostic criteria published in 2025 offer a framework for improving diagnosis.

The updated guidelines introduce several important changes.

For instance, the optic nerve (the nerve connecting the eye to the brain) is now included as a fifth anatomical location for assessing evidence of MS.

According to recent reports, the revised criteria also include new MRI biomarkers, such as the central vein sign and paramagnetic rim lesions. These features can help doctors distinguish MS-related abnormalities from other conditions.

These changes may help doctors diagnose MS earlier and more accurately.

According to recent reports, if you experience persistent or recurring neurological symptoms, seek medical advice. Your doctor can assess your symptoms and, if applicable, refer you to a neurologist.

Sudden weakness, vision loss, or difficulty speaking requires urgent medical assessment, Allder mentioned.

“Depending on the findings, investigations may include MRI scans of the brain and spinal cord, blood tests, and, in some cases, a lumbar puncture,” Allder noted.

“It is key that results are interpreted alongside symptoms and examination findings, as no single test should determine the diagnosis in isolation.”.

Allder stated that if you’re unsure about a diagnosis, you can ask your neurologist what evidence supports it and whether alternative health conditions have been considered.

“A second opinion or follow-up assessment may be appropriate. The priority is an accurate diagnosis that leads to the right treatment and support,” Allder mentioned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the past 17 months, the Wildlife Conservation Society’s Bronx Zoo in Latest York City has rescued dozens of parrots from the illegal pet trade. They include white-fronted Amazons (Amazona albifrons) and orange-fronted conures (Eupsittula canicularis).

The United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) confiscated the orange-fronted conures during three separate operations over the last 17 months, and the white-fronted Amazons in the last several months. All of the birds were discovered at the U.S.–Mexico border.

Industry observers note that “These animals were stolen from the wild and are victims of the illegal wildlife pet trade, and our responsibility is to give them the best possible chance for a healthy future,” Chuck Cerbini, WCS Bronx Zoo Curator of Ornithology, mentioned in a statement. “Working with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, our veterinary and animal care teams provide specialized expertise to assess, treat, and care for confiscated wildlife.”.

When confiscated wildlife arrives at the Bronx Zoo, the veterinary and animal care teams first conduct a health check, provide any necessary medical treatment, and then help find long-term placements for those that can’t be released into the wild.

White-fronted Amazons are native to parts of Mexico and Central America and represent the smallest Amazon parrot. They are also one of the few parrot species in which males and females feature visibly different plumage. Both sexes have a white foreheads, red faces, and yellowish bills, but males have red shoulders and females have green shoulders.

According to recent reports, orange-fronted conures, also known as half-moon conure or Petz’s conure, are also native to parts of Mexico and Central America, where they live in open woodlands, forest edges, and savannas. They have an orange forehead and green and blue feathers.

The IUCN Red List categorizes both birds as a species of Least Concern, but that still  doesn’t justify trafficking them in the illegal pet trade. Parrots throughout Latin America are subject to both the loss of forest habitat and poaching.

Birds in particular l are especially threatened by trafficking because they are valued in the pet trade and the collector trade.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Body recomposition is the fitness goal these days. If you’ve been hearing the term everywhere like I have, and thinking body recompo-what, you’re not alone.

Industry observers note that so, what is body recomp? Whether you knew it or not, chances are, you’ve probably pursued it at some point. If you’ve ever set out to reduce body fat or build muscle, you’ve been working toward a body recomposition goal. When people say body recomp these days, they really mean simultaneously losing fat and building muscle, not just one or the other.

Meet the expert: Brittany Busse, MD, is the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health.

Unlike simply losing weight, this approach isn’t about the number on the scale; it’s about improving the ratio of fat to muscle in your body for better health, performance, and aesthetics. (Oftentimes, when people talk about wanting to look "toned," they're really talking about body recomp, since you need low amounts of body fat to see the muscle you've built up.).

And, while body recomposition is completely possible, it can be a little more technical than other fitness goals. Here are the core things you need to know to get started on your body recomp journey.

Get started with our exclusive body recomp guide.

First: a quick refresher. Body composition refers to a percentage breakdown of how much body fat, lean mass (that is, muscle!), and bone you've got on your body. Body recomposition is the process through which you change that breakdown.

These are the five most crucial things to keep in mind when trying to make that happen.

At the most basic level, losing fat requires a calorie deficit; you need to burn more than you consume. Working with a nutritionist or doctor, you can determine exactly what this means for you, but for body recomposition, it's only a slight deficit that you should be shooting for. We’re talking 250 to 500 calories max.

Keep in mind: “Weight loss should not be confused with fat loss,” Brittany Busse, MD, the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health previously told Women's Health. “Much of weight loss can also be loss of muscle mass.”.

Sources indicate that and, you don't want to lose muscle mass, particularly if your goal is body recomp. That’s why protein is critical, Dr. Busse notes—but it’s just one piece of the puzzle. Tracking all three macros (protein, carbs, and fat) can go a long way in helping you stay full, energized, and strong while pursuing body recomp.

GET MORE INFO ABOUT COUNTING MACROS FOR BODY RECOMP WITH THE WH+ PDF.

Lifting is nonnegotiable. “People should weight train at least three times a week,” Dr. Busse remarked. “Weight training will build muscle mass, which will inevitably lead to improved metabolic health and fat loss.”.

In a recent development, keep up your cardio, too. But, if you’re a HIIT addict, you may want to try slowing things down. “Zone 2 cardio is the most effective way to burn fat while sparing muscle. This is exercising at a level where you can hold a ‘breathy’ conversation comfortably for 45-60 minutes,” Dr. Busse noted. “Walking on an incline, cycling, and rucking are all examples of Zone 2 workouts,” she said.

It's hard to come up with a training plan all on your own, so relying on the expertise of trainers to create a program can help make sure you're working your muscles efficiently and effectively.

Women's Health+ has many body recomp-focused programs for people of all experience levels: the 4-Week Walking Strategy, the 4-Week Strength Training Plan, the 4-Week Build & Burn Series (which allows you to follow along with dumbbell, barbell, or kettlebell-based workouts), and the Body Recomp Guide.

Age, hormones, and genetics all play a role in body composition, as does access to high-quality food and medical care. Not everyone has the same amount of time to spend exercising. So, take it easy on yourself, and if you can, get help and support as you work toward your goals.

It has been revealed that the longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home. That’s one of the big takeaways from the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) newly introduced “World Energy Outlook 2026,” which examines how the biggest oil supply shock on record could speed up the shift to EVs and solar.

It has been revealed that the world had a cushion at first when Trump kicked all this off with Iran. Well-stocked oil inventories helped buffer the initial shock, and the IEA coordinated a release of emergency oil reserves. Some Gulf oil took routes around the strait. Atlantic Basin exporters shipped more, and China sharply cut its crude imports. Now more of the burden is falling on consumers, who are paying higher prices and cutting back.

“While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be,” mentioned IEA executive director Fatih Birol.

The IEA has seen EV sales jump in some countries hit by the crisis, along with increased trade in solar panels and batteries. For countries that import a lot of oil and gas, switching to EVs and heat pumps can help reduce their exposure to the next fuel price spike.

Industry observers note that “The impact of Hormuz is only just beginning to become clear,” stated energy think tank Ember’s chief analyst Dave Jones. “Hormuz will speed up electrification and renewables, likely faster than many people think. So much of the momentum for electrification at COP31 comes from the desire to have cheaper and more secure energy.”.

According to recent reports, solar leads renewables growth in every scenario the IEA models, and nuclear power is growing strongly, too. Energy efficiency and biofuels could also gain ground. The push to use more homegrown energy could have a very different effect in parts of Asia, where some countries that import oil and gas have plenty of their own coal and could keep burning it for longer.

Recent findings suggest that the world was already using a lot more electricity before the crisis. Since 2019, electricity demand has grown twice as fast as overall energy demand, outpacing global economic growth. Everything from industrial motors and air conditioners to EVs, heat pumps, and data centers is driving that growth. Electricity comes close to 30% of the energy the world actually uses by 2035 in each of the IEA’s exploratory scenarios.

It has been revealed that before the crisis, around 20 million barrels of oil a day moved through the Strait of Hormuz. If shipping stays risky, newly introduced pipelines could route some of those barrels around the strait, while buyers turn to other suppliers or use less oil. In that case, the IEA states the amount of oil that needs to pass through Hormuz could drop to 8.5 million barrels a day in 2030 and below 2 million by 2035. The Middle East would still be the world’s largest oil-exporting region.

If the conflict is resolved, oil and gas supply could bounce back. A delayed wave of liquefied natural gas could also help bring prices down even as buyers refill their inventories. Faster electrification could take some of the demand out of both markets.

According to recent reports, the world is now using more energy to cool its buildings than to heat them for the first time, the IEA notes. By 2035, the global population is expected to grow by 650 million and the economy by a third. Energy needs rise gradually in advanced economies, growth slows in China, and India and Southeast Asia lead faster increases across other emerging and developing economies.

Then there’s AI. Under the IEA’s Stated Policies Scenario, global data center electricity use doubles to 1,000 terawatt-hours by 2030. That buildout is already running into grid and supply chain constraints, and in some places, local opposition. The IEA also flags risks to critical mineral supplies and threats to energy infrastructure from natural hazards and cyberattacks.

In a recent development, energy-related CO2 emissions stay around today’s levels under current policies. They start to fall under stated policies and drop further in the IEA’s Additional Response Case, which looks at what could happen if governments respond more strongly to the crisis. Even those deeper cuts fall short of what climate goals require. The current and stated policy scenarios point to 2.5C to 2.9C of warming, and the latest round of national climate pledges indicates little sign that countries are speeding up energy-sector emissions cuts.

The green agenda always come in a second place because people cannot see that far out in the future. Stability of the economy and energy independence are much more important drivers and have immediate impact. Local environment boosts like clean air in cities are also immediate drivers while long term reduced medical bills are not. The oil industry is challenged becuase, unlike previous numerous crises, there is an alternative and the green is the latest black.

There’s a more immediate cost, too. More people gained access to electricity and clean cooking in 2025, but higher fuel prices and shortages threaten to slow that progress. Around 720 million people still live without electricity, and nearly 2 billion cook with polluting fuels or technologies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the rarest and most coveted coins in United States history is headed for the auction block this week, where it could sell for over $2 million. But while collectors have long dreamed about owning one of the five existing 1885 silver trade dollars, the strange story of their creation remains murky more than 140 years after their minting.

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. struck the first trade dollars in 1873 as a way to compete with similar silver coinage in East Asia, but the production was short-lived. Silver market fluctuations and foreign policy shifts led to their demonetization in 1876, and they were only minted for collectors beginning in 1879. By 1884, the U.S. commissioned only 10 trade dollars before finally retiring the series destroying the die casts.

Industry observers note that however, a thoroughly corrupt political appointee named A. Loudon Snowden had other intends. Snowden’s career in currencies began in 1857, when his uncle and former Treasurer of Pennsylvania hired the then 22-year-old whippersnapper at the Philadelphia Mint. While at the mint, he pursued various personal profiteering interests, including the clandestine production and selling of thousands of rare coins for collectors.In 1885, Snowden finally retired as Superintendent of the Philadelphia Mint after nearly three decades.

It has been revealed that snowden also gave himself a parting gift before retiring—five 1885 trade dollars that he purchased from the Mint cashier. No one knew of their existence until a year after Snowden’s death in 1912. The first 1885 trade dollar auctioned in 1913 for $1,140 (about $32,174 in current valuation).

Although some numismatists and historians argue Snowden’s five trade dollars were a final grift, other experts argue that the coins have a surprisingly mundane backstory. Until the 1930’s, Mint employees were legally allowed to purchase examples of upcoming coinage for their equivalent amount. Snowden did just this when he previously bought 10 proof 1884 trade dollars, and it’s possible he bought the following year’s coins before the decision not to mint any others. Regardless of the true story, only five 1885 trade dollars exist today—and they’re worth far more than Snowden could ever imagine.

Stack’s Bowers will auction the 1885 trade dollar as part of its Rarities Night series on Tuesday, November 17.

Sources indicate that update 11/18/2026 12:50 p.m. EST: Stack’s Bowers confirmed its 1885 trade dollar sold for just over $1.95 million.
